'''Giacomo Bellacchi''' (1838{{endash}}1924) was an Italian [[mathematician]].<ref name="American Mathematical Society 1924">{{cite book |author=American Mathematical Society |title=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |publisher=Society |year=1924 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=h4XxAAAAMAAJ |access-date=7 October 2018 |page=571 |quote=Professor Giacomo Bellacchi, of the Technical School of Florence, died February 25, 1924, at the age of eighty-four years.}}</ref>

After graduating from [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]], he became a teacher at a military school and at the Tuscan Technical Institute, where one of his pupils was [[Vito Volterra]].<ref name="math-unifi">{{cite web | url=https://php.math.unifi.it/archimede/matematicaitaliana/biografie/tricomi/tricomi2.html | title=La matematica italiana 1800-1950 }}</ref>

Over his career, he carried out research both in [[geometry]] and [[algebra]]. He wrote many works, among which the most prominent is probably ''Introduzione storica alla teoria delle funzioni ellittiche (Historical Introduction to [[Elliptic Function]] Theory)'', which became well known and was used worldwide. He also wrote many university textbooks.<ref name="math-unifi" />

The library of the ''Fondazione Scienza e Tecnica'' in [[Florence]] has named after him its precious collection of math books and works.
